## Exact assumptions and conditional bounds

- [`sat26-general`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-general)
- [`sat26-reported-formal`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-reported-formal)

Conditional on `sat26-general`:

$$
2^{O(k\log\log k/\sqrt{\log k})}L^{O(1)}
$$

Alternatively, conditional on `sat26-reported-formal`:

$$
2^{O(k(\log\log k)^2/\sqrt{\log k})}L^{O(1)}
$$

The resulting algorithm is deterministic and uses polynomial space, conditional on the corresponding assumption and this derivation. $L$ denotes the original input length; constants may depend on the stated fixed constants. Logarithms in asymptotic bounds may be regularized when the declared measure is small.

## Preprocessing

Let G have n vertices. Compute any maximal matching and let C contain its endpoints. Put I = V(G) \ C. A matching of size q forces every vertex cover to contain at least q vertices, so |C| ≤ 2k. Maximality makes C a vertex cover; hence I is independent. This preprocessing is polynomial and does not require a minimum vertex cover. Handle an empty graph directly.

## Encoding size

| Quantity | Bound |
| --- | --- |
| Boolean variables, including auxiliaries | $O(k)$ |
| Clauses | $O(k^2)$ |
| Maximum clause width | $3$ |

## Derivation

1. Every clique uses either no vertex of I or exactly one vertex v of I. Consequently, $\omega(G)=\max\bigl(\{\omega(G[C])\}\cup\{1+\omega(G[C\cap N(v)]):v\in I\}\bigr)$, where the clique number of the empty graph is zero. Each graph in these subproblems has at most |C| ≤ 2k vertices.

2. For one such vertex set B and a threshold t, use one selection bit x_u for each u in B. For every nonedge uv of G[B], add $\neg x_u\vee\neg x_v$ directly. Add the linear-size cardinality circuit for $\sum_{u\in B}x_u\ge t$ from [METHODS.md, Section 2](../../METHODS.md). Thresholds outside [0,|B|] are handled directly.

3. The nonedge clauses enforce that the selected vertices form a clique, and the cardinality circuit enforces the threshold. Including all sum, carry, and comparison outputs, each query has N = O(k), M = O(k²), and width at most three. Nonedge clauses use existing selection variables and introduce no auxiliary variable per nonedge.

4. Binary search finds the clique number of each of the at most n+1 subproblems using O(log(k+2)) threshold calls. Retain a case attaining the maximum, including its outside vertex v when the case has one. The total number of calls at this stage is O((n+1) log(k+2)).

5. For the retained case, fix the optimum threshold and determine its selection bits one by one. Tentatively fix the next bit to zero; keep zero if the formula remains satisfiable and otherwise fix it to one. The current formula always has a satisfying extension, so this takes O(k) additional SAT calls. Add the retained outside vertex, if any, to recover an optimum clique of G. Only O(k) unit clauses are added.

6. All subproblem construction and graph access take polynomial time in the original input length L. Execute the queries sequentially. Their polynomial number and the O(k² log(k+2)) bit length of each nontrivial CNF are absorbed into the polynomial factor, giving the displayed conditional A(k) bound with polynomial space.

7. The maximal-matching argument and the clique decomposition above are self-contained catalog deductions. Sinz supplies background for the established cardinality technique; inclusion of this consequence is not a novelty claim.

## Caveats and comparison limits

- The displayed N and M bounds are per query; the algorithm makes polynomially many queries rather than joining all cases into one formula.
- The cover C computed from the maximal matching need not be minimum; the construction guarantees |C| ≤ 2k.
- The nonedge clauses can be quadratic in k. This route justifies the general-density A(k) profile, without a sparse B(k) claim.
- This entry is unweighted. It does not establish an FPT bound in clique size or a bound for binary-weighted Maximum Clique.

The derivation must preserve the objective and account for the encoding length of numerical values; a decision consequence alone does not establish the stated optimization bound.
